items.name: Yu Group
items.context: Reaction network theory for dose response
items.summary: Reaction network theory applied to targeted protein degradation
items.title: Undergraduate Researcher
items.org: Yu Group, Department of Mathematics, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
bullets: Originated and leads a project applying chemical reaction network theory and structural sensitivity analysis to steady-state dose response in targeted protein degradation systems.
Derived sensitivity equations and monostationarity conditions for open and closed kinetic models using the Feliu–Wiuf augmented Jacobian framework and Cramér’s rule.
Built symbolic and numerical tooling in Mathematica and Python (Tellurium) to validate analytical results against simulation.
First author on the resulting manuscript, in preparation.

items.name: MSK
items.summary: Lightweight LLM pipeline for CT chest radiology reports
items.title: Research Intern
items.org: Advanced Computing and Oncology Laboratory, Department of Radiation Oncology, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center
bullets: Developed a lightweight large language model pipeline that extracts thoracic cancer progression from CT chest radiology reports and runs on a personal computer without GPU acceleration.
Extended the same architecture to automate referral decision-making from radiology reports.
Conducted statistical analysis of the MSK-CHORD clinicogenomic dataset to identify molecular determinants of breast cancer metastasis.
Contributing to longitudinal immune profiling analysis for a thymus biomarker study using mixed-effects and joint longitudinal-survival models.

items.name: Wilson Lab
items.summary: Engineering modular protein therapeutics against oncogenic proteins
items.title: Undergraduate Researcher
items.org: Wilson Laboratory, Department of Microbiology, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
bullets: Engineering a class of novel modular protein therapeutics to efficiently translocate and selectively degrade oncogenic intracellular proteins.
Performed computational structure and solubility analysis using AlphaFold3, ColabFold, CamSol, GROMACS, and PyMOL to diagnose and resolve protein insolubility in chimeric constructs.
Carried out recombinant expression and purification by nickel affinity and ion exchange chromatography, with construct verification by Sanger sequencing and Western blot.
Functionally characterizing multiple homologs of a bacterial AB-type toxin to determine dimerization.
Developing modular immunotoxins to treat canine B cell lymphoma.
Mentoring seven undergraduate researchers; managing laboratory supplies and reagents and coordinating day-to-day laboratory operations.

items.name: BioAxis
items.summary: Mouse pose estimation on a foundation-model backbone, with DeepLabCut-format output
items.title: BioAxis
items.org: Foundation-backbone pose estimation for top-view mouse video
bullets: Standalone Python package for keypoint tracking in top-view mouse video: a label-free locator crops the animal, a pose model predicts the keypoints, and predictions are written in DeepLabCut's file format for use with existing downstream tools.

The pose model puts a heatmap head on a pluggable foundation backbone (DINOv2 by default, chosen in a backbone comparison), pretrained on the public TopViewMouse-5K dataset and fine-tuned on a small set of user-labeled frames.
Includes a desktop app and installer for collaborators, with tools to extract and label frames for further training.
Still in progress: temporal filtering beyond a median filter, model ensembles, and evaluation on datasets outside the pretraining set.

items.name: CRNDose
items.summary: Dose-response monotonicity analysis for general reaction networks
items.title: CRNDose
items.org: Dose-response monotonicity for general mass-action reaction networks
bullets: Aims to generalize the analysis in “Structural constraints on non-monotonic dose response in targeted protein degradation networks” from the degrader network to an arbitrary mass-action reaction network, given a dose and an output species.

Being built to return a steady-state verdict (monotone, monotone under stated conditions, or non-monotonicity permissible) with a machine-checkable certificate; the symbolic steady-state analysis is sound but incomplete, and transients are treated numerically.
Planned stack: Python with SymPy, NumPy/SciPy and Tellurium, with regression tests against the manuscript's results.

items.name: LabFoundry
items.summary: Web-based system for managing, running and tracking lab protocols
items.title: LabFoundry
bullets: Web-based system for managing, executing, and tracking laboratory protocols across a research group.
Separates version-controlled protocol templates from individual protocol runs; a finalized template is immutable and an edit creates a new version.
Role-based access: admins create and finalize templates and approve members' requests to run a protocol.
Protocols are run step by step, recording per-step timestamps, deviation notes and an outcome; experimental data stays elsewhere and is linked by reference.
